text:
sam: heads-up — after landing prompt-affinity packing yesterday we see a small p99 regression on short-seq workloads, ~12% higher than baseline. anyone else seeing this?
ana: saw the alert, digging in. can you share which kernel paths triggered?
devon: I profiled a sample trace. kernel selector prefers fp16-fast-gemm when batch width >= 48, but with affinity packing batches are narrower and more skewed, so selector fell back to mixed-precision fallback that is slower for short sequences.
sam: interesting. so affinity packing reduced overall batch count but increased kernel mismatch for small batches?
matt: yup. affinity tries to keep same prompt prefixes together which creates highly uneven token budgets per work item. you get fewer but thinner batches.
laura: example numbers from yesterday's perf run (10k requests, short seq avg 48 tokens):
```
baseline: p99=120ms, tokens/sec=95k, avg_batch=52
affinity-opt: p99=135ms, tokens/sec=100k, avg_batch=39
```
sam: tokens/sec went up slightly but tail latency worse — tradeoff looks like throughput vs tail SLA. what's the KV-cache hit behavior in these traces?
devon: KV cache hit-rate went from 18% -> 42% (good). but hits shorten runtime per item and create more prefix-length variance in the queue. the scheduler then forms batches by affinity which amplifies variance.
nana: can we adjust token-budget target or max-wait to prefer slightly wider batches for short-seq models?
matt: experimented with bumping token_budget_target from 256 to 384 and increasing max_wait_ms from 6 to 10. result: avg_batch back to ~48, p99 improved to ~122ms but tokens/sec dropped ~3%.
laura: config used:
```
batching:
  strategy: prompt_affinity
  token_budget_target: 384
  max_wait_ms: 10
  prefer_wider_batches_for_short_seq: true  # experimental
```

sam: looks reasonable. do we have kernel selector heuristics to prefer GEMM-fast even for narrower batches when sequence lengths are tiny?
devon: kernel selector currently uses batch_width * seq_len cost estimate. we could add a bias term for avg_seq < 64 to favor certain GEMM kernels. simple patch I sketched: if avg_seq < threshold and batch_width < w_thresh, add -alpha to estimated cost for fp16-fast-gemm.
nana: suggest we run A/B: 10k requests each, short and long seq traffic mixes, check p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and KV-hit fairness. also check GPU util and kernel occupancy traces.
laura: I ran occupancy dump for affinity-opt: many kernels showing low SM occupancy for 30-50 token cases. matches fallback kernels being used.
matt: one more twist: when KV hits are high, effective remaining tokens drop mid-batch which can bork continuous batching heuristics; we should verify admission control that re-evaluates token budgets when a hit inflates prefix length.
sam: action items: 1) devon to push kernel-selector bias patch and a canary config (token_budget_target 384, max_wait_ms 10) 2) ana to run A/B with short/long mixes and capture traces + occupancy 3) laura to validate KV-hit telemetry and ensure batch re-eval points are logged 4) matt to add a metric showing "batch_kernel_mismatch_rate" so we can quantify when selector falls back.
devon: I'll send a tiny PR with selector tweak and a flag gate. PR will include perf script. hoping to land in next deploy.
nana: tagging @matt for dashboards and @infra-bot to kick an experiment run when PR is in.
infra-bot: experiment scheduled: exp-id=exp-2026-03-18-09, canary cluster=affinity-canary-3, traffic-split=10/90, duration=30m. logs will be in /runs/exp-2026-03-18-09/
sam: great. if the bias reduces p99 by >6% without hurting tokens/sec >5% we'll flip by default. otherwise revert. :thumbsup:
laura: adding one more note — watch out for regression on long-seq because bias may over-prefer GEMM for long workloads. include long-seq gate in A/B.
matt: ack. I'll add dashboard panels for long-seq p99 and kernel occupancy.
nana: cool. I'll post results in this thread when experiment finishes.
sam: thanks team — solid debugging.
